en.heading: 8 March: Philippine National Women's Day is a working special holiday
en.origin: Philippine National Women's Day highlights women's contributions to public life and work and creates opportunities for institutions to celebrate and discuss gender equality. Republic Act No. 6949, approved in April 1990, established 8 March each year as a special working holiday; the statutory text does not grant a general day off. The law encourages employers and public bodies to allow participation in workplace celebrations; it is distinct from the March Women’s Role in History Month proclaimed in 1988.

en.heading: 29 October: a separate Indigenous Peoples Thanksgiving Day
en.origin: National Indigenous Peoples Thanksgiving Day calls public attention to the rights and historical contributions of indigenous cultural communities throughout the Philippines. Proclamation No. 486, signed on 13 October 2003, established 29 October annually, reflecting the date when Republic Act No. 8371, the Indigenous Peoples Rights Act, was approved in 1997. The single-day observance preceded National Indigenous Peoples Month, introduced in October 2009; they share a rights context but have separate acts, scopes and origins.

en.heading: 22 April: the Philippines' Earth Day acquired an annual decree in 2008
en.origin: The Philippines' Earth Day on 22 April is part of the wider international environmental-awareness movement and promotes activities addressing ecological damage and community protection. The country's presidential precedents include Proclamation No. 553 for Earth Day 1990 and Proclamation No. 1276 for Earth Day 2007; each designated a particular year's observance. Proclamation No. 1481 of 10 April 2008 established 22 April of every year as the Philippine observance and designated the environment department to coordinate activities; this annual decree is not the origin of global Earth Day.
en.promoter: Department of Environment and Natural Resources with public agencies and community partners are the relevant public or institutional bodies for this legally documented Philippine day and its civic programmes.

en.heading: 3 April: founding of the National Commission for Culture and the Arts
en.origin: The NCCA establishment anniversary marks the creation of the Philippines' principal public commission for supporting cultural and artistic development across the country's diverse communities. Republic Act No. 7356 was approved on 3 April 1992 and created the National Commission for Culture and the Arts together with a national endowment fund for cultural and artistic work. The statute recognizes culture as a human right and emphasizes pluralism and broad participation; its institutional anniversary is not the same origin as Museums and Galleries Month, created in 1991.

fr.origin: L'anniversaire de la NCCA rappelle la création de l'institution publique chargée de soutenir le développement culturel et artistique des communautés philippines. La loi de la République nº 7356, approuvée le 3 avril 1992, a créé la Commission nationale pour la culture et les arts et un fonds de soutien culturel. La loi reconnaît la culture comme droit humain et défend le pluralisme; l'anniversaire institutionnel diffère du Mois des musées de 1991.

de.heading: 3. April: Gründung der Nationalkommission für Kultur und Kunst
de.origin: Der NCCA-Gründungstag erinnert an die Einrichtung der öffentlichen Kommission zur Förderung kultureller und künstlerischer Entwicklung in den Philippinen. Republikgesetz Nr. 7356 vom 3. April 1992 gründete die Nationalkommission für Kultur und Kunst und einen staatlichen Förderfonds. Das Gesetz versteht Kultur als Menschenrecht und betont Vielfalt und Teilhabe; die Gründung ist nicht mit dem Museumsmonat von 1991 gleichzusetzen.

pt.heading: 3 de abril: criação da Comissão Nacional da Cultura e das Artes
pt.origin: O aniversário da NCCA recorda a criação da comissão pública para apoiar desenvolvimento cultural e artístico nas comunidades filipinas. A Lei da República n.º 7356, aprovada em 3 de abril de 1992, criou a Comissão Nacional da Cultura e das Artes e um fundo nacional de apoio cultural. A lei reconhece a cultura como direito humano e valoriza pluralismo e participação; o aniversário é distinto do Mês dos Museus de 1991.
